title: 这块芯片为什么有餐盘大？
title_en: Why Is This Chip the Size of a Dinner Plate?

segments.zh: Why is this AI chip
the size of a dinner plate?
Line up fifty nine of them,
and they run a three trillion parameter AI.
segments.en: 就能跑一个三万亿参数的AI。

segments.zh: Cerebras says it can write up to two thousand tokens a second.
segments.en: Cerebras说，一秒能吐上千到两千个词元，

segments.zh: That's pages of text, every second.
Today's question:
why does a bigger chip make AI faster?
segments.en: 芯片做大，AI为什么就变快？

segments.zh: Meet Chippy.
A normal chip, about as big as a postage stamp.
segments.en: 一块普通芯片，跟邮票差不多大。

segments.zh: Chippy does math insanely fast.
Trillions of multiplications a second.
But here's the catch:
most of the time, Chippy is waiting.
Waiting for what?
For numbers to arrive from memory.
Picture a chef who cooks in one second,
segments.en: 想象一个厨师，一秒就能炒好菜，

segments.zh: but the fridge is down the hall.
To write each word, an AI must read
a huge pile of its numbers from memory.
segments.en: 都要把一大堆参数从内存读一遍。

segments.zh: It's like running to the fridge
for every ingredient of every dish.
segments.en: 每样食材都得跑一趟冰箱。

segments.zh: So the speed limit isn't the cooking.
It's the walking.
Engineers have a name for this:
the memory wall.
For years, chips got faster at math
segments.en: 这些年芯片算得越来越快，

segments.zh: much faster than memory got at delivering.
Twist one:
what if the fridge sat right on the counter?
segments.en: 要是冰箱就在灶台边呢？

segments.zh: That's the Cerebras idea:
don't cut the silicon wafer into little chips.
Keep the whole wafer:
one giant chip, about twenty centimeters on a side.
segments.en: 一块巨大的芯片，边长二十多厘米。

segments.zh: Memory sits right beside every tiny core.
segments.en: 内存就贴在每个小核旁边，

segments.zh: Forty four gigabytes on one wafer.
The ingredients are within arm's reach.
No more hallway.
Twist two:
forty four gigabytes still isn't enough.
Even at four bits per number,
the model weighs about one and a half terabytes.
That's about sixteen gigabytes per layer,
and there are ninety three layers.
So build an assembly line:
each wafer holds one or two layers.
Wafer one runs its layers,
then hands the result to wafer two.
Only small results travel between wafers.
segments.en: 晶圆之间只传小小的中间结果，

segments.zh: The heavy numbers never move.
Each hop takes about two microseconds.
One blink fits tens of thousands of hops.
If the heavy numbers had to travel too,
segments.en: 要是参数也得搬来搬去，

segments.zh: we'd be right back in the hallway.
Twist three, the sneaky one:
while wafer two works, wafer one starts the next request.
segments.en: 第二片在忙，第一片已经开始下一单。

segments.zh: Like a car factory:
lots of cars on the line at once.
segments.en: 流水线上同时好多辆车。

segments.zh: A fifty nine station line
serves lots of people's questions at the same time.
segments.en: 同时处理好多人的问题。

segments.zh: Count them: twenty four wafers for the big layers,
thirty five for the light ones. Fifty nine.
The light layers keep a small fixed notebook,
segments.en: 小层只记一个固定大小的小本子，

segments.zh: so two of them can share one wafer.
The result: for a model this huge,
the target is one to two thousand tokens a second.
segments.en: 目标一秒一千到两千个词元。

segments.zh: For comparison: when you read,
you manage maybe four or five words a second.
What it writes in one second
would take you several minutes to read.
Friendly fine print: this is the company's own blog.
segments.en: 友情提示：这是公司自己的博客，

segments.zh: It's a deployment plan, not an independent test.
segments.en: 例子是一份部署方案，还没有第三方实测。

segments.zh: And a whole wafer is hard to make.
It carries spare cores to route around defects.
segments.en: 它得留备用的核，绕开坏点。

segments.zh: So the secret isn't just bigger.
segments.en: 所以秘诀不是越大越好，

segments.zh: It's stop running to the fridge.
Inside computers, moving data
often costs more than doing the math.
So next time your AI answers instantly,
thank the chef who never leaves the kitchen.
segments.en: 谢谢那个从不出厨房的厨师。

elements.text: a chip the size of a plate
